definition: To succeed in reaching a goal, usually after effort over time.
example: She achieved a perfect score only after months of daily practice.

definition: The way someone thinks and feels about something, shown in how they behave.
example: His attitude towards deadlines changed once he joined a larger team.

definition: To think about something carefully before deciding.
example: The council will consider three different sites before choosing one.

definition: A change that happens because of something else.
example: The medication had no measurable effect on his blood pressure.

definition: To set something up so that it lasts, or to prove that something is true.
example: The company established its first office abroad in 1994.

definition: Facts or signs that show whether something is true.
example: There is little evidence that the policy reduced traffic at all.

definition: The reason something is done, or what it is meant to do.
example: The purpose of the survey was to find out why members were leaving.

definition: Large or important enough to be worth noticing.
example: There was a significant drop in applications after the fee was introduced.

definition: The place, person or thing that something comes from.
example: The report never names the source of its figures.

definition: To admit that something is true, or to show you have noticed someone.
example: The manufacturer finally acknowledged that the fault was its own.

definition: To produce a change in something, or to influence how it develops.
example: Rising fuel prices affect almost every part of the economy.

definition: To accept that something is true without checking it.
example: Do not assume the data is accurate simply because it was published.

definition: An advantage gained from something.
example: One benefit of the new schedule is that nobody travels during rush hour.

definition: Large in amount or degree, enough to matter.
example: Rebuilding the archive took considerable time and money.

definition: To be the parts that something is made of, or to count as something.
example: Women constitute nearly two thirds of the workforce in this sector.

definition: To decide something officially, or to be the factor that decides an outcome.
example: Rainfall in early spring largely determines the size of the harvest.

definition: Happening at once, without any delay.
example: The new rule had an immediate effect on how staff recorded their hours.

definition: Money that a person or organisation regularly receives, usually from work.
example: Households on a low income were hit hardest by the price rise.

definition: Certain to happen and impossible to prevent.
example: Given how quickly the ice is retreating, some flooding is inevitable.

definition: To keep something in the same condition, or to keep saying something is true.
example: The bridge is expensive to maintain but far too useful to close.

definition: To change something slightly, usually to improve it or make it fit.
example: Engineers modified the design after the first round of testing.

definition: Easy to see or understand, needing no explanation.
example: The reason for the delay was obvious the moment we saw the queue.

definition: To make something smaller in size, amount or degree.
example: Switching to rail reduced the company's emissions by a third.

definition: To need something, or to officially demand it.
example: The course requires no previous knowledge of statistics.

definition: As much as is needed.
example: Suspicion alone is not sufficient grounds for an investigation.

definition: A habit of behaving in a certain way, or a general direction of change.
example: There is a tendency to blame the software when the process is at fault.

definition: Found over a large area or among many people.
example: The practice was widespread long before anyone tried to regulate it.

definition: Enough for what is needed, though not more than that.
example: The lighting was adequate for reading but too dim for detailed work.

definition: Covering everything that is relevant, leaving nothing out.
example: The inspectors produced a comprehensive account of what went wrong.

definition: To say or show the opposite of something else, so both cannot be true.
example: The new figures contradict everything the earlier study concluded.

definition: One of several things that together cause a result.
example: Cost was only one factor in the decision to close the branch.

definition: To suggest something without stating it directly.
example: Her silence seemed to imply that she disagreed with the plan.

definition: To give a good reason for something, showing it was right or necessary.
example: The board could not justify the expense to its members.

definition: To notice something, or to understand it in a particular way.
example: Younger customers perceive the brand quite differently from older ones.

definition: Unwilling to do something, and slow to agree to it.
example: Investors remain reluctant to fund projects with no clear return.
